newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello says interest rate prospects good.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello says interest rate prospects good.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday that prospects for economic growth through the rest of 1997 were very strong by world standards and that prospects for interest rates were also good.
"All the indications are that growth throughout 1997 is going to be pretty strong by world standards," Costello told reporters after a cabinet meeting to discuss Australia's high unemployment.
He said the government was forecasting GDP growth of 3.75 percent in the year to June 30, 1998, which was better than either Europe or the United States.
"So it's strong growth out there, but you've got good inflation prospects, good interest rate prospects," he said.

Last week the Reserve Bank of Australia cut official cash interest rates for the fifth time since mid-1996 by 50 basis points to 5.00 percent. Economists on average say there is 30 percent chance of another rate cut.

"What people want to see is long sustained growth. They're not interested in five minutes of growth, five minutes of recession. We want long sustained growth and that's what our economic strategy is directed towards producing," he said.
He had been asked what was needed to foster the confidence needed to boost growth.
Costello later said he expected the unemployment rate to fall through the rest of 1997 from its current 8.5 percent and be at or a little below 8.00 percent by the end of June 1998.
The government forecast in its May budget that the unemployment rate would be 8.00 percent by the June quarter of 1998.
